matchstick.title: Movable vertical sticks in simple numerals
matchstick.principle: I, II, III, and L consist only of vertical matchsticks, so adding or removing a single vertical stick from them yields another valid Roman numeral (e.g., I→II, II→I, L→I).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to adjust a numeral's value by ±1 and the numeral is one of these simple forms.
matchstick.example: Changing II to I by removing one vertical stick.

matchstick.title: Preserve source and destination validity
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, both the character you removed it from and the character you added it to must still be recognized Roman numerals or allowed operators.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Always check the validity of both the source and target after any stick move.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical from '+' yields '-', which is still a valid operator.

matchstick.title: Guide moves by numeric difference
matchstick.principle: Compute the numeric values of both sides of the equation; the difference tells you how much the total must change, guiding which stick moves (±1, ±2, etc.) are needed.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving, to prioritize candidate moves that can bridge the numeric gap.
matchstick.example: If left side is 4 and right side is 11, you need a net change of –7 on the right.

matchstick.title: Reordering I around V changes value by 2
matchstick.principle: Moving an I from before V (IV = 4) to after V (VI = 6) or vice‑versa changes the numeral’s value by exactly 2.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the required adjustment is a multiple of 2 and the equation contains IV or VI.
matchstick.example: Changing IV to VI adds 2 to the value.

matchstick.title: Cross‑side vertical stick transfer adjusts both sides by ±1
matchstick.principle: Removing a vertical stick (I) from a numeral reduces its value by 1; adding that stick to a numeral on the opposite side of the equation raises its value by 1, changing the total balance by 2.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric gap is even and you can afford to change both sides by one.
matchstick.example: Moving an I from VII (7) to IV (4) yields VI (6) and V (5), altering the equation by 2.

matchstick.title: Never take sticks from V or X
matchstick.principle: V and X are built only from diagonal sticks; removing a diagonal leaves an invalid shape, so they cannot be sources for stick moves.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a candidate move involves taking a stick from V or X, discard it.
matchstick.example: Taking a diagonal from V would leave a single diagonal, which is not a Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Operator validity after stick moves
matchstick.principle: Operators must remain one of the allowed symbols (+, -, =). Removing the vertical from '+' turns it into '-', which is valid; other modifications that produce non‑allowed symbols must be avoided.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a stick move involves an operator, verify that the resulting operator is still permitted.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical line from '+' yields '-', a valid operator.

matchstick.title: Final verification of numerals and equality
matchstick.principle: After performing a stick move, re‑evaluate each token to ensure it is a valid Roman numeral or operator, then compute the arithmetic to confirm the equality holds.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the end of the solving process, before submitting the answer.
matchstick.example: Check that IV = VIII – IV evaluates to 4 = 4.

matchstick.title: Operator‑to‑numeral vertical stick transfer
matchstick.principle: A vertical stick can be moved from the '+' operator to a numeral, converting '+' into '-' and adding an I to the numeral, which raises its value by 1; similarly, moving a vertical from '-' to a numeral turns '-' into '+' and adds an I.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is off by a small amount and you need to both change the operator and increase (or decrease) a numeral by 1, consider moving the vertical stick from the operator to that numeral.
matchstick.example: Changing VII + IV to VIII – IV by moving the vertical from '+' to VII.

matchstick.description: Taking a stick from V or X, leaving an invalid shape
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes any stick can be removed, overlooking that V and X consist only of diagonal sticks which cannot form a valid numeral when missing one.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Never select V or X as a source for a stick unless you also add a diagonal to create another valid shape; treat them as non‑removable.

matchstick.description: Changing an operator to an invalid one
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model moves sticks from operators without checking the resulting symbol, sometimes producing symbols not in the allowed set (+, -, =).
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After any operator modification, verify that the new symbol is one of the permitted operators.

matchstick.description: Assuming a single stick can change a numeral's value arbitrarily
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model overestimates the effect of moving a stick, ignoring the limited ways a numeral can be altered by one stick.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Recall the specific value changes each allowed stick move can produce (e.g., ±1 for I, ±2 for IV↔VI).

matchstick.description: Neglecting to recompute the arithmetic after the move
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes declares a solution without verifying the resulting numeric equality.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always recalculate the left‑ and right‑hand side values after the move and confirm the equality.

matchstick.description: Treating diagonal sticks as interchangeable with vertical sticks
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model conflates stick orientations, moving diagonal sticks where only vertical ones are allowed (or vice versa).
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Respect stick orientation: vertical sticks can only become I‑type components; diagonal sticks belong to V or X and cannot be used as I.
